summary.headline: Fino Payments Bank Q2 FY27 revenue rose 9% QoQ to INR 333.6 crore but fell 17% YoY, with EBITDA at INR 35.1 crore (10.5% margin).
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue of INR 333.6 crore was up 9% sequentially and down 17% YoY, with H1 revenue around INR 640 crore (down 25% YoY) on recalibration of the B2B P2M business. Net revenue was INR 127.1 crore (down 14% YoY, up 3% QoQ) with net revenue margin of 38.1%, and EBITDA fell to INR 35.1 crore from INR 43.1 crore in Q1 and INR 61.6 crore a year earlier. Deposits, CASA accounts and loan referral disbursals kept growing, while the SFB transition timeline was reiterated as on track for Q1 FY28 go-live. Management declined to give FY27 guidance, calling it a transition year.

segments.name: CASA / liability franchise
segments.commentary: CASA contributed about 52% of revenue (INR 174 crore), including a record renewal income of INR 74.6 crore; renewal income is guided at INR 65-75 crore per quarter. Management says 90% of deposits are core balances and 99% are savings account balances.

segments.name: Loan referral
segments.commentary: Q2 disbursals INR 762 crore and H1 INR 1,390 crore; current run-rate about INR 250 crore per month. Referral is currently purely referral with underwriting done by partners; pipeline targets gold loans, affordable housing, loan against property and secured MSME.

segments.name: CMS / B2B alliances
segments.commentary: CMS throughput INR 20,511 crore, up 12% YoY, but pricing competition continues to weigh on take rates. Monthly CMS collections exceed INR 6,500 crore, about 60% for NBFCs, banks and MFIs.

segments.name: Traditional transactions (AEPS, remittance)
segments.commentary: AEPS and remittance recovered 50% and 18% sequentially, respectively, on higher DBT activity. UPI B2B P2M relaunch is targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Treasury
segments.commentary: Fund management yields about 100 bps above market yields despite FY26 rate cuts, per management.

guidance_outlook: No guidance given for FY27; management called it a transition year focused on regaining volumes and SFB preparation.
SFB go-live targeted for Q1 FY28 per Slide 12; management would not comment on RBI timelines.
Cost of funds expected around 4% post SFB conversion, retaining a 250-300 bps advantage over traditional SFBs.
Capex of INR 120-150 crore over 12-15 months post SFB transition, mainly technology (LOS, LMS, collateral management, enterprise NPA).
Around INR 2,000 crore of disbursals targeted in first 12 months of SFB operations; INR 8,000-10,000 crore book targeted over 3-4 years.
Approximately 40 liability branches and 25-30 asset centres planned in first year; about 125 existing branches and contact points to convert.
Corporate BC business exit to be executed before applying to RBI, per plan.
Cash@UPI and AEPS-based products are fee-based and not subject to MDR; MDR timing is uncertain.
capex_capacity: SFB capex INR 120-150 crore over 12-15 months post transition, largely technology.
Branch plan to be firmed up by Q4 FY27 before applying to RBI.
Around 3,000 existing employees; asset-vertical hiring to follow RBI final approval.
Four senior executives hired for branch banking, liabilities, credit risk and MSME lending; PwC supports programme and operational readiness.
demand_pricing: Digitally active customers 64.9 lakh in September 2026; 87.9 lakh in the quarter.
8.2 lakh new accounts in Q2, roughly one every 10 seconds.
Competition in B2B/CMS continues to pressure pricing; Q1 B2B and alliance volumes fell after a reputational event, with recovery in Q2.
Cash@UPI launched; NPCI three-party cash deposit product backed by AEPS launched at Global Fintech Festival 2026.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management of SFB go-live in Q1 FY28, and could RBI cause delays?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is tracking the timetable on Slide 12 but cannot comment on RBI's timelines.

qa_highlights.question: How does MDR (pushed to January) help from Q3 onwards?
qa_highlights.answer: Tejas Maniar said MDR timing is uncertain and guidance will follow once it is implemented; partner discussions are ongoing.

qa_highlights.question: Are gold loan stresses seen in the referral book?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said underwriting sits with partners and current data show no skepticism from underwriters, though it is too early to judge.

qa_highlights.question: How will a deposit book that moves like transactional float fund assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Agarwal said 90% of deposits are core and 99% are savings balances, which are sticky; the SFB opening balance is INR 2,500-3,000 crore per the questioner.

qa_highlights.question: What are the medium-term revenue, EBITDA and RoA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Agarwal declined to give FY27 guidance and called the year a transition period.

qa_highlights.question: Is INR 2,000 crore first-year disbursal target too conservative given H1 referral of INR 1,390 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Anup Agarwal said it is a realistic first-year target to test guardrails; the book is expected to reach INR 8,000-10,000 crore in 3-4 years, and the number could change over the next three quarters of referral activity.

risks_watch: EBITDA fell to INR 35.1 crore from INR 61.6 crore a year ago; management says investment in people, technology and process will weigh on short-term profitability.
Pricing pressure in CMS/B2B alliances continues to erode take rates.
MDR timing uncertain; referral underwriting sits with partners; gold loan stress questions unresolved.
Deposit-led lending depends on the transition from payment bank restrictions (INR 2 lakh balance cap) and on branch rollout, with no quantification given.
Corporate BC business exit and branch plan (due Q4 FY27) remain open items before RBI application.
summary.management_tone: Confident on liabilities, CASA and the referral franchise, but cautious and non-committal on guidance, timing of MDR and RBI approval. Management repeatedly declined to quantify FY27 outcomes and called the year a transition period.
key_quotes: FY27 remains a transition year, and our priorities are unchanged.
Our cost of funds for Q2'27 was 1.4%, giving Fino a structural cost advantage.
So I think it's too premature to comment on whether the gold loan will come under stress for us currently.
As it will be the first year of operations. We want to test the guardrails, which we have built, the processes we have built when we go live.

growth.why: No FY27 numeric guidance was given (management declined, calling it a transition year), so growth is unguided; the SFB go-live (Q1 FY28), about 2,000 crore year-1 disbursals and 40 branches/25-30 asset centres are planned, with a INR 120-150 crore tech capex that is only partly backed by specifics, while Q2 revenue fell 17% YoY.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Net revenue margin H1 at 40.3% vs 35.2% a year ago, but Q2 margin fell 450 bps QoQ to 38.1% and EBITDA margin is 10.5% (INR 35.1 crore vs INR 61.6 crore YoY), with management flagging investment weighing on short-term profitability; MDR timing uncertain so upside is not assured.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: SFB go-live targeted for Q1 FY28 with about 40 liability branches and 25-30 asset centres planned in the first year, though the branch plan is only firmed up by Q4 FY27 and RBI timing is not commented on.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 CASA added 8.2 lakh accounts, loan referral disbursals reached INR 762 crore in Q2 (+286% YoY, run-rate about INR 250 crore/month), and CMS throughput rose 12% YoY, but revenue fell 17% YoY and no FY27 volume guidance was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: SFB tech capex of INR 120-150 crore over 12-15 months is already anticipated and the branch plan is due by Q4 FY27 before the RBI application.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management declined to give any FY27 revenue, margin or RoA guidance and called the year a transition period, with Q2 revenue down 17% YoY.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: EBITDA fell to INR 35.1 crore from INR 61.6 crore YoY and opex is rising (Q2 +5.8% YoY), with pricing pressure in CMS and uncertain MDR timing, though no formal guidance exists to cut.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: UPI B2B P2M relaunch is targeted by Q4 FY27 and NPCI three-party cash deposit product (AEPS-backed) is already launched; Cash@UPI is live.

rows.label: SFB transition go-live
rows.why: Timetable on Slide 12 targets Q1 FY28 go-live with cost of funds around 4% and a 250-300 bps advantage over traditional SFBs, but management would not comment on RBI timelines.

rows.label: Year-1 SFB disbursal target
rows.why: Management targets around INR 2,000 crore of disbursals in the first 12 months of SFB operations versus H1 FY27 referral of INR 1,390 crore, with an INR 8,000-10,000 crore book targeted in 3-4 years.

rows.label: CMS/B2B pricing pressure
rows.why: Competition in B2B/CMS continues to erode take rates even as CMS throughput grew 12% YoY to INR 20,511 crore.

tone.note: Management was confident on CASA, deposits and the referral franchise and SFB timetable, but cautious and non-committal on FY27 guidance, MDR timing and RBI timelines; analysts pressed on guidance, MDR, gold loan stress and the first-year disbursal target.
